original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Write out the p = 2 instance of PR288's FO lemma on Lambda/pLambda for the full lower Borel in PR288's superposition register model (PR288 open item 3), with applied free maps allowed to be singular mod 2 and only the data block of the final state fixed: sum of paid ranks >= sum_w rank((g_w mod 2)_HD) = mW on unit targets; remark on m = 1 for any rational data; exact finite checks.
scope_change_reason: Seed 9 (bit track). The card asks whether a larger or nonabelian register model escapes the three-register obstruction; PR288 lists the full nonabelian Borel model (free D += K*H) as open item 3. Review showed the 2-integral case is an instance of PR288's own FO-on-Lambda/pLambda tool, so the note is scoped as a corollary that narrows item 3 to data outside Z_(2).
bottleneck_link: On unit targets, locates where a small-width bit saving in the superposition Borel model must come from: an applied matrix (paid frame or free map) with an even denominator; 2-integral words on targets that are not units mod 2 get only a weaker bound and normalise to n_I only through dyadic free maps.
stop_rule: Stop after the corollary, its proof, and exact finite checks of each lemma with scope controls and mutation-tested positive controls; no search over dyadic data.
evidence: PROOF.md: nu_pi = rank of the H x D block of pi (PR288's FO functional on Lambda/2Lambda, P1's nu) is subadditive, 0 on mixing and block-lower maps (even singular mod 2), <= rank A on paid shears, and sum rank (g_w mod 2)_HD on the data block. verify.py: 90 homomorphism products, 18 forced F2 cancellations, 96 random words (864 steps, 74 free maps singular mod 2), 8 positive controls reaching the target exactly at cost mW (direct, Levi- and Borel-conjugated with K != 0), data-block controls, 384 steps of the m = 1 mod-p module check on dyadic words, 4 scope controls; shipped --mutations mode rejects 8/8 injected defects.
author: Sagar Thakrar
ai_assistance: Prepared with substantial AI assistance: Claude Code (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5) wrote the proof, verifier and text; AI reviewers audited it. No independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: At m = 2, can the full Borel model (with D += K*H) save with data outside Z_(2)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is PR288's open item 3 after this note; the abelian and G0 models never save at m = 2.
open_questions.first_step: The smallest instance: W = 2, three rank-one paid calls, one inserted D += K*H, rational data; compare the abelian dyadic floors of PR1604/PR1679 and PR2085/PR2112.

open_questions.question: Where does PR589's bit saving leave Z_(2) when written in this model?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If PR589's local frame path is a rational-frame XOR word of this kind, it saves on unit targets and so must use an even denominator; locating it would show which frames carry the saving.
open_questions.first_step: Express one PR589 local frame path as an element of GL_16(Q) and read off its denominators.
open_questions.blocked_by: A precise map from the E8 frame formalism into the register model.
